How to save a Base64 image to a file

Decode the image’s Base64 payload back to bytes, check its actual format, then download the original file. A complete PNG example below lets you follow the process from a data URL to a working image.

By ParseCove · Published 27 November 2026

On this pageSave the imageComplete sampleData URL or raw Base64?JavaScript & PythonTroubleshootingTerms & FAQ

Save a Base64 image in four steps

  1. Get the complete value. Copy either the raw Base64 payload or the full data:image/...;base64, URL. Leave out surrounding JSON quotes, HTML markup and ellipses.
  2. Open the image converter. Paste the value into Base64 to image and press Preview image. The tool accepts PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP image bytes.
  3. Check the preview and detected format. Confirm the dimensions and file type. If the declared media type disagrees with the bytes, the viewer explains the mismatch and uses the detected format for the download.
  4. Download the original image. Use Download original image and keep its detected extension. The download restores the encoded file bytes; it does not resize, recompress or convert image formats.

The current viewer limits a file to 10 MB and a preview to 40 megapixels. A byte signature alone does not prove that a whole file is intact: the browser must also be able to decode it.

Check the original file’s SHA-256

For this sample, compare the downloaded file with this complete checksum:

dc538cbd93118bb8c291a38f1c12a3e71f5d84257e435ae81971eb14653490d3

This identifies the exact sample bytes. It is not a general safety or file-authenticity check.

Data URL and raw Base64 are different inputs

A Base64 image data URL contains a header and a payload separated by a comma. The header declares a media type and the ;base64 encoding flag. A raw Base64 string contains only the encoded bytes.

Header layout — the complete sample is above

data:image/png;base64,
PartPurposeWhat to paste
data:Identifies a data URLKeep it when using the full data URL.
image/pngDeclares the media typeIt describes the data; changing it does not change the bytes.
;base64,Marks the encoding and ends the headerKeep the comma. A decoder expecting raw Base64 needs only the part after it.
Payload after the commaEncodes the original file bytesCopy the whole payload, including any final padding.

Data URLs can also contain percent-encoded data without a Base64 flag. This tutorial and the image viewer cover the Base64 form. Raw Base64 is useful when an API asks for encoded file content without a data URL prefix.

References: MDN: data URLs · RFC 2397: the data URL scheme.

Save the sample with JavaScript or Python

The examples below write the complete PNG sample without turning its binary bytes into UTF-8 text. They check the PNG signature; they are not full image-file validators. For unknown input, use the viewer’s format detection and browser preview as well.

JavaScript: run in this guide’s browser console

const dataUrl = document.querySelector('#save-image-sample').value;
const prefix = 'data:image/png;base64,';
if (!dataUrl.startsWith(prefix)) throw new Error('Expected the PNG sample.');
const payload = dataUrl.slice(prefix.length).replace(/\s/g, '');
const binary = atob(payload);
const bytes = Uint8Array.from(binary, char => char.charCodeAt(0));
const signature = [137, 80, 78, 71, 13, 10, 26, 10];
if (!signature.every((value, i) => bytes[i] === value)) {
  throw new Error('The bytes do not have a PNG signature.');
}
const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes], { type: 'image/png' }));
const link = document.createElement('a');
link.href = url;
link.download = 'parsecove-example.png';
link.click();
setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);

atob() produces a binary string. Converting each character to a byte before constructing the Blob preserves the image bytes. Writing that binary string as ordinary UTF-8 text can change bytes above 127.

Python 3: run, then paste the copied sample at the prompt

import base64
from pathlib import Path

data_url = input("Paste the complete PNG sample data URL: ").strip()
prefix = "data:image/png;base64,"
if not data_url.startswith(prefix):
    raise ValueError("Expected the PNG sample.")
payload = "".join(data_url[len(prefix):].split())
image_bytes = base64.b64decode(payload, validate=True)
if base64.b64encode(image_bytes).decode("ascii") != payload:
    raise ValueError("Non-canonical Base64.")
if not image_bytes.startswith(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"):
    raise ValueError("The bytes do not have a PNG signature.")
Path("parsecove-example.png").write_bytes(image_bytes)

The Python example writes a binary file with write_bytes(). Its strict decoder checks characters and padding; the round-trip check also rejects non-canonical trailing bits.

References: MDN: atob and binary strings · Python: Base64 decoding.

Why a Base64 image will not open

For alphabet, padding or UTF-8 errors, use the Base64 troubleshooting walkthrough to separate encoding validation from interpreting the bytes.

SymptomCheck
Invalid characters or paddingCopy the original value again. Remove only its surrounding markup, not arbitrary characters. A truncated payload cannot reliably be repaired by adding = signs.
Text decoder says the bytes are not UTF-8Image bytes are binary. Use the image viewer rather than a Base64-to-text decoder.
The header says JPEG but the bytes are PNGUse the format detected from the bytes. Renaming the file or editing the media type does not convert it.
The file starts like an image but preview failsThe image may be truncated or otherwise invalid. A correct opening signature is only one check.
An API returned - and _ charactersIt may be Base64URL. Inspect it with the Base64URL decoder and copy the standard Base64 representation before using this image viewer.

SVG and other image types are outside this viewer’s current preview support. A failure here does not mean every data URL or every browser supports the same formats.

Terms used in this guide

Data URL
A value beginning with data: that includes the content itself. Data URI is an older name often used for the same form.
Media type
A label such as image/png describing the intended content format. Also commonly called a MIME type.
Payload
The data after the comma. In a Base64 image data URL, it is the encoded image-file content.
File signature
Opening bytes associated with a format. A signature check helps identify a type but does not validate every part of a file.

Common questions

Can I save the Base64 text directly as image.png?

Saving the encoded characters as a .png file does not restore the image. Decode the payload and write the resulting bytes. The filename extension alone does not change the content.

Can Base64 decoding turn a PNG into JPEG?

No. Decoding restores the original encoded file bytes. Changing image formats requires decoding pixels and re-encoding them with an image editor or a format-conversion library.

Should I copy the data URL or only its payload?

This image viewer accepts either. For another API or library, check its expected input. Many Base64 decoding functions want only the payload after the comma.

Does every data URL use Base64?

No. The ;base64 flag is optional in the data URL syntax. Without it, the content can use percent encoding. The examples here deliberately use the Base64 image form.
